intro: Here in Aydın province lies Aphrodisias, an ancient city whose story reaches back to the 2nd century BC. It is a Roman city that stood beside its own marble quarries, and it became famous for its school of sculpture.
history: Aphrodisias grew around the cult of Aphrodite, and its loyalty to Rome was rewarded with exemption from tax. Its sculptors worked the local marble and sent their statues across the empire. Imagine the ring of chisels from the workshops of this city.
structure-1: You are now in the Stadium, the best-preserved stadium of the ancient world. Look around: both ends are still standing, and thirty rows of seats run the whole way round. It lies inside the city walls, tucked against their northern edge.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Aphrodite and the Tetrapylon, then the Sebasteion and the sculpture workshops where this city's fame was carved.
facts: Did you know? The 30,000-seat stadium is the best-preserved stadium surviving from antiquity, and both of its curved ends are still standing. The Sebasteion reliefs show Roman emperors beside gods — the fullest surviving programme of imperial propaganda carved in stone. The marble quarry lay just two kilometres away. And the signatures of Aphrodisian sculptors turn up from Rome to North Africa.
outro: This brings our journey through Aphrodisias to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This marble has outlived its sculptors by centuries; let it outlive us too. Enjoy your visit.
